//telemetry: Key `telemetry.scope` controls which command tiers wrap Task dispatches in span-start/span-end telemetry (scripts/skailr/emit-telemetry.mjs). Default is "program-only": /yolo-program, /build-program, /discover, /plan-program, /continue-program keep telemetry on (a long multi-workstream run is where span-level visibility earns its keep); /patch and /yolo skip it by default — real campaign data (docs/BENCHMARKS.md) showed span wrapping adds 2 Bash calls per dispatch across 6-7+ dispatches on a typical single-feature run for a signal (subagent cost attribution) that was itself broken until this same pass fixed it in bench/. Set "scope": "all" to re-enable everywhere, or "scope": "off" to disable entirely. See .claude/skills/emit-telemetry/SKILL.md and .claude/program/schemas/telemetry-event.schema.json. install.sh copies this file only if absent, so your override survives upgrades.
//autoUpdate: Key `autoUpdate` defaults to enabled here ("autoUpdate": { "enabled": true }), so scripts/skailr/check-update.mjs checks npm at most once per 24h and prints a one-line notice when a newer skailr-agents exists. It never upgrades anything. To opt out, set "autoUpdate": { "enabled": false }. install.sh copies this file only if absent, so your override survives upgrades.
//note: Hooks used to live in this file and never fired — Claude Code doesn't auto-load custom-named settings files, only .claude/settings.json / .claude/settings.local.json / ~/.claude/settings.json. Hooks moved to .claude/settings.json (2026-08-08). This file keeps its original, narrower job: consumer-preference toggles that install.sh preserves on upgrade rather than overwriting.
